6. **Memory and call size.** The compaction candidates under "Call size matters as much as call count", chosen from the per-section breakdown measured in item 1: older letters summarized with the ledger of promises keeping what matters, by the seat's own model (a cheaper one may take over later, after the cheap test in "A cheaper model for condensing"), a "since you last acted" view, terser state tables, and ordering requests so the stable part is cached; and the output side ("Output is the other half"): the engine writing what it can, envoys passing words on as written by a flag, a cap on each job's output and no free-text reasoning fields. Measure before and after. First, the new ending ("Random ending" under Victory, revised 20 October 2026): any season may be the last from the first, with the chance growing so the median game ends in 1332 BCE, and the hard cap drawn in secret from 80 to 100 seasons, as its first guess says, both settings in the setup menu with these as their defaults (the cap a range from which the engine draws the real season in secret, or none); the last season itself drawn once in secret at the start, from its own seeded stream, and read by nothing shown, the omens included; the open age, a setting with no end at all ("An open age" under Victory); and the first year moves from 1345 to 1346 BCE ("Calendar"), in the interface's date labels and wherever else a year BCE is shown. The rulebook, the seat view and the web app's ending line (today "the age cannot end before …" and the phone header's "Can end from …") say it in words, without numbers. Also routine audiences answered by a cheaper model ("Routine audiences are answered by a cheaper model"), measured the same way, with how often audiences are passed on to the seat's own model. Measure the style tell and journal leaks that entry names too. Light alerts are routed the same way ("Light alerts go to the cheaper model too"), measured by how often the cheaper model wakes the seat's own model and whether it missed anything that mattered. With routine audiences comes "Every model is the table's choice": the setup menu sets a provider and a model for each job (kings, characters, the narrator, routine audiences, sorting, summaries and planning), any seat able to override its job's choice, Sonnet and Haiku by default, everything on Opus possible, routine audiences possible to turn off, planning off by default, and the choices recorded in the log. With them comes the rest of "Minds follow what is at stake" (revised 27 October 2026): the ladder of script, small and large model for every job, the worth of a call judged decision by decision, a budget or a target spent where calls matter most, passing up and asking advice from a brief, phrasing calls, audits, presets, standing answers and one call per wake-up, for kings and characters; city-states and vassals join in item 11+. And the rest of "Scheduled, conditional orders" under Pacing, since sleeping kings live on their standing orders: "unless" conditions, conditions on the treasury, an envoy's return or a sealed tablet, all in the structured, engine-checkable vocabulary.

   **Built in three parts** (decided 26 October 2026, the third split from the second on 27 October), each its own pull request with its own stop for review:
   - **6a. The ending and the table.** The last season drawn once at the start, the cap and the median as settings, the open age, the first year moved to 1346 BCE, and the ending said in words. **Stop for review.**
   - **6b. Call size.** First, Haakon's answers to item 6a's review (27 October 2026): an open age with model seats asks for its spending limit by hand ("An open age"), and the table's median reaches every seat in words, script kings included ("What kings are told" under "Random ending"). Then compaction and the output side, the rest of scheduled, conditional orders, standing answers with their phrasing calls, and one call per wake-up ("Minds follow what is at stake"), each measured before and after. Built after 6a. **Stop for review.**
   - **6c. Who decides** (split from 6b on 27 October 2026). Every model the table's choice, with planning as an option, presets and unpriced models shown as unknown on the cost meter ("Every model is the table's choice"); the ladder of script, small and large model for every job, with routine audiences and light alerts as its first cases, passing up and asking advice from a brief; and the worth of a call, the budget or target, and audits ("Minds follow what is at stake"), for kings and characters alike. The machinery is tested with stand-in repliers; what it saves is measured in the model games after the build order. Built after 6b. **Stop for review.**
